title: Audio file: convert, measure, draw a waveform, report

turns.prompt: {D}/tone.wav is a 90-second stereo recording. Convert it to Ogg Vorbis as {D}/tone.ogg, render a waveform image of it to {D}/waveform.png, and write {D}/media-report.md with the duration in seconds (one decimal), the sample rate, the channel count and the output file sizes. Then give me the duration and sample rate.
turns.seed:
mkdir -p {D} && python3 - <<'EOF'
import math, struct, wave
w = wave.open('{D}/tone.wav', 'wb'); w.setnchannels(2); w.setsampwidth(2); w.setframerate(22050)
n = 22050 * 90
fr = bytearray()
for i in range(n):
    v = int(12000 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * 440 * i / 22050) * (0.5 + 0.5 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * i / (22050 * 6))))
    fr += struct.pack('<hh', v, -v)
w.writeframes(bytes(fr)); w.close()
EOF
turns.verify: cd {D}; test -f tone.ogg || { echo FAIL: no tone.ogg; exit 0; }; test -f waveform.png || { echo FAIL: no waveform.png; exit 0; }; test -f media-report.md || { echo FAIL: no report; exit 0; }; d=$(ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of csv=p=0 tone.ogg 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-5); m=$(head -c 8 waveform.png | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n'); echo "SHOW ogg_duration=$d png_magic=$m"; sed 's/^/SHOW /' media-report.md | head -20; case $d in 89.*|90.*) ok=1;; *) ok=0;; esac; if [ $ok = 1 ] && [ "$m" = 89504e470d0a1a0a ]; then echo PASS; else echo FAIL: duration=$d png=$m; fi

rubric.criteria: Report states ≈ 90.0 s, 22050 Hz, 2 channels and the output sizes; the reply gives the duration and sample rate.
